headline: PAGASA Warns of Heavy Monsoon Rains Over Zambales and Bataan as LPA Nears Northern Luzon
seoTitle: PAGASA: Heavy Habagat Rains Over Zambales, Bataan | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA warned of monsoon rains over Zambales and Bataan on August 28 as a low pressure area east of Itbayat continued to enhance unsettled weather across Luzon.
deck: Zambales and Bataan face heavy to intense monsoon rains and elevated flash-flood and landslide risk while PAGASA monitors a low pressure area east of Itbayat, Batanes.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA warned Friday morning that Zambales and Bataan would experience monsoon rains as the Southwest Monsoon continued to affect Luzon and Visayas.

In its 4:00 AM forecast on August 28, PAGASA located a low pressure area about 720 kilometers east of Itbayat, Batanes at 3:00 AM. The weather bureau said the combination of the LPA and Habagat was maintaining unsettled conditions across large parts of Luzon.

sections.heading: Where the heaviest rain is expected
paragraphs: PAGASA classified Zambales and Bataan under monsoon rains, with possible flash floods or landslides due to heavy to intense rainfall. Metro Manila, the Ilocos Region, Abra, Benguet, Tarlac, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Bulacan, Rizal, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, Oriental Mindoro and Antique were forecast to receive occasional rains.

The approved FMB News morning brief also cited regional PAGASA rainfall warnings for parts of western Luzon. Because rainfall-warning levels are updated frequently, residents should follow the latest regional PAGASA bulletin for their locality rather than rely on an earlier warning color after conditions change.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: PAGASA's weekly outlook had already projected occasional rains over Zambales, Bataan and Occidental Mindoro through August 28 because of Habagat. Its selected-city outlook showed a 100% chance of rain in the Subic Bay-Olongapo area on Friday, with monsoon rains expected during the weekend.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rainfall over already saturated ground can trigger rapid flooding and slope failures even where rainfall temporarily weakens. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation and road-closure instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: PAGASA continues to monitor the LPA east of Northern Luzon. Forecasts and rainfall-warning levels may change quickly as the disturbance evolves and interacts with the Southwest Monsoon.
